In the 'Human Last Test' (HLE) with tool use, Qwen3-Max-Thinking scored 58.3, outperforming GPT-5.2-Thinking (45.5) and Gemini 3 Pro (45.8), achieving the highest score among all models. The model also significantly enhances native Agent capabilities, enabling intelligent, adaptive tool use—such as search, personalized memory, and code interpreter—through joint reinforcement learning with rule-based and model-based rewards. This allows for professional-level responses with reduced hallucination. The model is currently available for free via QwenChat, with API access through Alibaba Cloud's Model Studio, and will soon be integrated into the Qwen app, offering all users free access to the most powerful version of the Qwen series. The announcement was published on January 26, 2026, by DriveHome (Kuaizhijia).

articles.title: 2025: The Year AI Reasoning Models Took Over  --  A Month-by-Month Review of Frontier Breakthroughs
articles.summary: In 2025, AI reasoning models achieved transformative progress, shifting from parameter scaling to advanced 'thinking' capabilities. Key breakthroughs occurred monthly: Gemini 2.5 Pro (March) introduced deep thinking and 1M-token context; OpenAI's GPT-4.5 (April) emphasized deliberate reasoning tiers; DeepSeek R1 (May-June) led an open-source reasoning surge with strong math performance and low training costs; Grok 4 (July) surpassed human expert levels on GPQA Diamond (88%) and AIME 2025 (93%); GPT-5 (August) reached 94.6% on AIME and 88.4% on GPQA, with multi-tier pricing and robust tool use; September saw a cross-lab SOTA race with GPT-5, Grok 4, and Gemini 2.5 Pro leading on composite benchmarks; October-December brought Gemini 3 Pro Preview, Claude 4.5, and open-weight models like Llama 4 and Qwen 3, enabling frontier performance across enterprise and open ecosystems. On benchmarks, models now exceed human performance on AIME (up to 95%), GPQA (88.4%), and coding (SWE-bench ~75%), but remain sub-human on open-ended scientific reasoning, long-horizon planning, and real-world accountability. Key architectural innovations included deliberate 'thinking' modes, Mixture-of-Experts efficiency, multi-million-token contexts, and agentic tool use, redefining AI from chatbots to 'AI employees.'

articles.title: From Being Underestimated to Musk's Praise: Chinese AI Models Rewrite Industry Rules with 'Intelligence Density'
articles.summary:
The AI industry is undergoing a fundamental shift from a parameter-scale arms race to an efficiency-driven revolution centered on 'intelligence density,' triggered by the release of Alibaba's Qwen 3.5 series. Elon Musk praised the models on social media with the comment 'Impressive intelligence density,' while MiniMax founder Yan Junjie identified 'intelligence density' as a core strategic pillar during a financial report conference call. This pivot follows a reflection on the 'scaling laws' that dominated the sector for three years, where trillion-parameter models and 100,000 GPUs were the benchmarks. However, a cover study by the Liu Zhiyuan team at Tsinghua University, published in 'Nature Machine Intelligence,' revealed a paradox: for every tenfold increase in model parameters, performance gains may be less than 20%, while computational costs grow exponentially. 

Liu Zhiyuan's proposed 'density law' offers a new framework; backtesting of 51 mainstream models showed that from 2023 to 2025, the intelligence density of large models doubled every 3.5 months. This implies that every 100 days, humans can achieve equivalent performance with half the parameters, a rate of efficiency improvement far exceeding the traditional Moore's Law. IBM Chief Scientist Kaoutar El Maghraoui stated, '2026 will be the watershed between efficient models and frontier models.'

The practical performance of Qwen 3.5 confirms this leap: a 9B parameter model scored 81.7 on the GPQA Diamond test with an instruction-following accuracy of 91.5%, and a 0.8B micro-model can handle a context of 260,000 tokens, equivalent to running two or three full-length novels simultaneously. These capabilities, previously requiring server clusters, can now be deployed on ordinary smartphones. The Qwen team released 9 open-source models in 16 days, establishing dominance in their respective parameter categories. MiniMax, a company with an average employee age of 29 and 385 staff, achieved a 159% revenue growth and a 437% gross margin increase with a $500 million investment. Yan Junjie emphasized that the organizational leverage effect from increased intelligence density far exceeds simple resource stacking.

The explosion of edge computing power provides the material basis for this shift. The Liu Zhiyuan team calculated that in 2023, the total edge computing power scattered across various devices in China was 12 times that of data centers. With 9B models achieving performance levels ten times that of their parameter count, AI deployment thresholds have dropped from server clusters to consumer-grade graphics cards, and startup entry costs have fallen from '$1 billion in financing' to '300 engineers.' This is dismantling the technical barriers and pricing systems established by giants like OpenAI.

Industry anxiety is evident in comments by the Anthropic CEO, a tech leader known for an anti-China stance, who has recently frequently accused Chinese models of 'gaming the rankings through rote learning.' However, Musk's endorsement exposes the fragility of this rhetoric; when competitors achieve similar performance through more efficient technical paths, the premium models of traditional giants face a fundamental challenge. The API price for GPT-3.5 level models has plummeted 266.7 times in 20 months, validating this industrial trend of technical deflation.

In this efficiency revolution, Chinese companies show unique competitive advantages. The entire Qwen 3.5 series is open-sourced under the Apache 2.0 protocol, a strategy that contrasts sharply with the technology blockade by US giants. As 9B models can run complex AI tasks on mobile phones, the process of technology democratization is irreversible. As Professor Liu Zhiyuan predicted, 'As long as a certain intelligence can be realized, it will inevitably run on smaller terminals in the future.' This ultimate form of distributed intelligence may be the true essence of the 'dense intelligence' praised by Musk.

articles.title: HKUST Professor's AI Glasses Experiment: 92.5 Score in 30 Minutes Beats 95% of Students
articles.summary: A team led by Professor Zhang Jun and Meng Zili from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology conducted an experiment testing the performance of AI-powered smart glasses, specifically the Rokid Glasses, integrated with the GPT-5.2 large language model during a final undergraduate exam for the course 'Principles of Computer Networks.' Students wearing the glasses took the exam by looking down at the test paper, with the glasses' camera capturing images of the questions. The images were transmitted via a 'glasses-phone-cloud' pathway to a remote AI model for analysis and reasoning. The AI-generated answers were returned through the same route and displayed clearly on the glasses' screen. The entire reasoning process took only 0.8 seconds, allowing students to copy answers efficiently. The test participant achieved a score of 92.5 in just 30 minutes, ranking in the top 5 out of over 100 students, significantly surpassing the class average of 72. Although the highest-scoring student achieved 97.5, they required 3 hours, highlighting the AI's superior speed. The research team evaluated 12 mainstream commercial smart glasses, including those from Meta, Xiaomi, and Rokid, selecting Rokid Glasses for their higher development flexibility. The device features a Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 chip, weighs only 49 grams, includes a 12MP Sony IMX681 camera, and dual Micro-LED waveguide displays. The software used was GPT-5.2, which achieved a 92.4% accuracy rate on the GPQA Diamond PhD-level scientific reasoning test and a perfect 100% score on the AIME 2025 math competition benchmark. The AI scored full marks on multiple-choice and single-page questions and most points on multi-page questions; errors occurred mainly due to sub-questions being split across different pages, preventing the AI from viewing all information at once. The team noted that incorrect answers were primarily from highly complex, reasoning-intensive questions, indicating the model's strong partial reasoning ability even when the final answer was wrong. During the test, Wi-Fi transmission of high-resolution images significantly increased power consumption, reducing battery life from 100% to 58% within 30 minutes, underscoring ongoing challenges in power efficiency and connectivity stability of smart devices. The experiment has sparked debate in the education sector about the future of traditional assessment methods, as AI now demonstrates consistent high performance on standardized exams. Institutions are already adopting AI proctoring tools that use eye-tracking, background noise monitoring, and writing style analysis to detect cheating.

articles.title: GTP 5.2 vs Gemini 3: How both AI platforms stack against each other | Mint
articles.summary: OpenAI launched GPT 5.2 on December 12, 2025, positioning it as its most advanced AI model series to date for professional and enterprise use, in response to growing competition from Google's Gemini 3. According to OpenAI, GPT 5.2 Thinking achieved a new high score on the GDPval evaluation, meeting or exceeding human expert performance in over 70% of 44 occupational tasks, delivering results at more than eleven times the speed and less than 1% of the cost of professional labor. Early testers reported improvements in formatting, design sophistication, and structural coherence in documents like spreadsheets and slide decks. The model also demonstrated enhanced coding capabilities, including better bug detection, feature implementation, and refactoring of large codebases, with notable gains in front-end development—especially for complex, 3D interfaces. On long-context reasoning, GPT 5.2 achieved near-perfect accuracy on the four-needle MRCR evaluation at a 256,000-token context window, enabling effective analysis of lengthy documents such as legal contracts and research papers. On LMArena, GPT 5.2 High ranked second in web development tasks, behind Claude Opus 4.5, with Gemini 3 Pro in fourth; however, GPT 5.2 is not yet listed on broader leaderboards. Benchmark comparisons show a mixed outcome: OpenAI claims GPT 5.2 outperforms Gemini 3 on GPQA Diamond and AIME 2025 (without tools), while Google reports higher scores for Gemini 3 on multimodal benchmarks like MMMLU and certain reasoning tasks. Independent evaluations from groups such as ScaleAI have not yet included GPT 5.2.
